title: The Smallest Odd Abundant Number Coprime to 3 Is 5391411025
description: An axiom-free Lean 4 capstone proving IsLeast {n | Odd n ∧ ¬3∣n ∧ Abundant n} 5391411025 — the least odd abundant number not divisible by 3 is exactly 5391411025 = 5²·7·11·13·17·19·23·29. Both directions: the witness is itself odd, coprime to 3, and abundant (via multiplicativity of σ, no native_decide), and no smaller such number exists (a sharp rational Euler abundancy argument reducing to four explicit 7-prime supports and forcing 25∣n, 49∣n).

overview.historicalContext:
**Abundant numbers and the role of small primes.**

A positive integer n is abundant when σ(n) > 2n (the sum of its proper divisors exceeds n). The smallest abundant number is 12, and the smallest odd abundant number is 945 = 3³·5·7 (sibling entry abundant-number-oq-02). The factor 3 is doing heavy lifting there: forbidding it forces the smallest example to leap from 945 to the eight-prime number 5391411025 = 5²·7·11·13·17·19·23·29, whose abundancy index σ(n)/n ≈ 2.00306 only barely clears 2. Odd numbers coprime to 3 are 'only just' abundant, which is exactly what makes the extremal value so large and the proof so delicate.
overview.problemStatement:
**The open question (abundant-number-oq-02-oq-01).**

What is the least element of S = { n | Odd n ∧ ¬(3 ∣ n) ∧ Nat.Abundant n }?

**Answer: 5391411025 = 5²·7·11·13·17·19·23·29.**

This entry is the capstone that proves IsLeast S 5391411025 in Lean, combining a witness-membership certificate with the minimality lower bound established across the companion files.
overview.text: An axiom-free Lean 4 proof that the smallest odd abundant number coprime to 3 is exactly 5391411025, stated as IsLeast over the family of odd abundant 3-free integers.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Two halves, assembled.**

1. **Membership (upper bound)**: 5391411025 is odd, not divisible by 3, and abundant. Abundance is checked via multiplicativity of σ — σ(5391411025) = σ(5²)·σ(7)·σ(11)·σ(13)·σ(17)·σ(19)·σ(23)·σ(29) = 31·8·12·14·18·20·24·30 = 10799308800 > 10782822050 = 2·5391411025 — so no divisor enumeration over a ten-digit number is needed (and no native_decide).
2. **Minimality (lower bound)**: every odd abundant n coprime to 3 satisfies n ≥ 5391411025. This is the hard half, assembled in the companion files from the squarefree case (≥ 33426748355), the ω ≥ 8 case (≥ 5391411025), and the residual ω = 7 case. The ω = 7 case pins the prime support to one of four explicit sets {5,7,11,13,17,19,q}, q ∈ {23,29,31,37}, via a sharp rational Euler abundancy product, then forces 25 ∣ n and 49 ∣ n and bounds the magnitude.
3. **Assembly**: witness_mem_lowerBounds repackages the minimality theorem as an order-theoretic lower bound, and isLeast_oddThreeFreeAbundant pairs it with the membership certificate to produce IsLeast S 5391411025.
keyInsights: **IsLeast is the right headline shape**: stating the result as IsLeast S 5391411025 captures both the upper bound (the witness is in S) and the lower bound (nothing smaller is) in a single Mathlib-idiomatic statement, matching the sibling entries smallest_abundant (12) and the odd case (945).

**Multiplicativity beats enumeration**: abundance of a ten-digit number is reduced to eight one-line divisor-sum computations via isMultiplicative_sigma, so the proof never touches a divisor enumeration of 5391411025 and stays free of Lean.ofReduceBool / native_decide.

**The minimality half was already done, just not packaged**: the prior companion files proved odd_abundant_coprime_three_ge_witness (≥ 5391411025) and, separately, mem_odd_three_free_abundant (the witness is in S). The main file's header still called minimality 'the open half'; this capstone observes that it is closed and assembles the two into the exact-minimality IsLeast.

**Razor-thin abundance**: σ(n)/n ≈ 2.00306 — the abundance margin is only 16486750 out of ~5.4·10⁹ — explaining both why the extremal value is so large and why the lower bound needs sharp (not just supremum) Euler weights.

conclusion.summary: This capstone resolves the open question abundant-number-oq-02-oq-01 in full: the least odd abundant number coprime to 3 is exactly 5391411025 = 5²·7·11·13·17·19·23·29, stated as IsLeast over the family of odd abundant 3-free integers and proved axiom-free. It assembles the witness-membership certificate (abundance via multiplicativity of σ, no native_decide) with the minimality lower bound built across the companion files (sharp rational Euler abundancy argument reducing the ω = 7 residual to four explicit prime supports and forcing 25∣n, 49∣n).
conclusion.implications: The result completes a small family of exact extremal-abundancy theorems alongside the least abundant number (12) and the least odd abundant number (945), and demonstrates that ten-digit abundance certificates are tractable kernel-checked facts when σ is assembled multiplicatively rather than by divisor enumeration. The lower-bound machinery (sharp per-prime-power Euler weights, refined_euler_set, the residual-support analysis) is reusable for other constrained least-abundant questions, e.g. coprime-to-15 or higher congruence restrictions.
